doc.title: Paquito D'Rivera — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Claudio Roditi and the Brazilian influence on his writing
summary: Roditi's Brazilian knowledge changed how he composed and led him to work with many Brazilians.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young

blocks.x: So, Claudio brought a different sound to your band.
Did it encourage you to write in a different way?

Yes, that also, because of the knowledge of the Brazilian music. I think in Brazilian many times, many times. Quite literally, I use the Brazilian part very often; I have become like an honorary Brazilian. The [imitates rhythm] that type of Brazilian thing which you hear, the way the tambourine music [imitates sound/rhythm], that type of pattern, I use in my mind to compose music, to compose melodies. Not all the time, but on many occasions. That is in, said to understand thanks to Claudio Roditi because when he enter my band, I start working more and more with Brazilians. I had a Brazilian also and Michel Camilo who was Dominican, but he know the Brazilian stuff very well, as well as the Venezuelan stuff. So it is that mixing of a lot of music in Latin America in my group. That was the intention, but mainly Brazilian; I love the music of Brazil.
